## 主要学术背景 | Scholarly background

**中文。** 欧洲接触后传染病造成的美洲人口崩溃是殖民史和生物考古学的核心问题，但长期主要依赖文献、人口模型和间接病理证据。古病原体基因组学能够直接识别感染个体，并比较古代病毒与后来的全球谱系，从而把“哪一种病原体何时进入美洲”转化为可以由分子证据检验的问题。

**English.** The demographic collapse associated with post-contact epidemics is central to colonial history and bioarchaeology in the Americas, but it has long been reconstructed mainly from documentary sources, demographic models and indirect pathological evidence. Ancient pathogen genomics can identify infections directly and compare ancient viruses with later global lineages, turning questions about which pathogens entered the Americas and when into testable molecular problems.

## 主要发现 | Major findings

**中文。** 研究从智利北部Camarones 9两名印加—殖民时期个体中重建出美洲最早的古代天花病毒基因组，年代约为公元1492–1631年。病毒属于一个现已灭绝的谱系，其分化时间晚于中世纪欧洲早期毒株、早于现代variola谱系形成。

**English.** Researchers reconstructed the first ancient smallpox genomes from the Americas from two Inca-Colonial individuals at Camarones 9 in northern Chile, dating to approximately AD 1492–1631. The viruses belong to an extinct lineage that split after early medieval European strains but before modern variola lineages emerged.

## 学术重要性 | Intellectual significance

**中文。** 美洲接触后疾病造成的人口灾难长期主要依赖历史文献和人口学推断。这项研究首次提供病原体本身的直接分子证据，把“天花何时、以何种谱系进入南美洲”转化为可由古基因组检验的问题，也使殖民史、疾病史与考古人群研究真正结合起来。

**English.** The demographic catastrophe caused by post-contact disease has long been reconstructed largely from documentary and demographic evidence. These genomes provide direct molecular evidence for smallpox introduction into South America and connect colonial history, pathogen evolution, and archaeological human remains.

## 学术出版物 | Academic publications

Romero GonzÃ¡lez, B., Reyes-Madrid, M., Arriaza, B., Cassidy, L. M., Moraga, M., la Fuente Castro, C. d., & Nakagome, S. (2026). The genomic identity of early smallpox in South America. Science, 393(6810), 504â508. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aee6957

**出版物内容（中文）。** 文章从智利北部 Camarones 9 两名早期殖民时期个体中重建出美洲最早的古代天花病毒基因组，并将其置于全球 variola 病毒系统发育树中。结果为欧洲接触后天花进入南美洲提供病原体本身的直接分子证据，并显示早期美洲毒株属于后来消失的谱系。

**What the publication shows (English).** The study reconstructs the earliest ancient smallpox genomes yet recovered in the Americas from two early colonial individuals at Camarones 9 in northern Chile and places them within the global variola phylogeny. It provides direct molecular evidence for the introduction of smallpox into South America after European contact and shows that the early American viruses belonged to an extinct lineage.
